To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The key to successful calving management is accurate calving prediction, moving cows to maternity units on time, discrete supervision and knowing when and how best to intervene.

“Cows that have been milked in the 24 h prior to parturition and are moved to a calving pen on time have a reduced incidence of dystocia and retained fetal membranes, and a reduced need for intervention, and have a higher milk production in the following lactation”.
The incidence of dystocia in dairy cattle is approximately 10% and the most common causes are uterine torsion and pelvic fracture.
